**About 300 W of solar recharges a 1,000 Wh power station from empty in one good day. A 200 W panel does it in roughly a day and a half.**

**The formula**

Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × real-world efficiency of about 0.7 to 0.75)

| Conditions | Panel watts for a full recharge in 1 day |
|---|---|
| Summer, about 5 peak sun hours | ~270-300 W |
| Average US day, 4-4.5 peak sun hours | ~320-340 W |
| Northern winter, about 2 peak sun hours | ~735 W |

Sources for these figures: [Power Runtime](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/) (340 W at 4 sun hours, 270 W at 5) and [Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/) (about 300 W in summer, about 735 W in a northern January).

**If you're fine with a slower recharge**

- A 200 W panel gives about 630 Wh on an average day, so it refills 1,000 Wh in about 1.5 days ([Watt48](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station), [Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- Power Preflight's rule of thumb is to divide the battery's Wh by 5, which gives about 200 W for a 1,000 Wh unit.
- A 100 W panel takes around 3 days.

**Check before you buy**

- **Solar input limit:** Every station caps the watts it accepts. Mid-range 1,000-1,500 Wh units typically allow 400-800 W, but some accept only 200 W, and panels beyond the cap add nothing ([Held in Reserve](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge)).
- **Voltage:** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc), and the combined Voc if you wire panels in series, must stay inside your station's input window. Going over can damage the charge controller ([Power Preflight](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).
- **Connectors:** Panels usually have MC4 connectors, while stations often use XT60 or DC barrel plugs, so you may need an adapter cable.
- **Using power while charging:** Net charge is solar input minus your load, so recharging will be slower if you're running devices.
- **Aiming:** Tilting panels toward the sun and re-aiming them a few times a day can add 20-30%.

If you tell me which power station you have, I can check its solar input limit and suggest a panel that fits.

One of the search results was a retailer page for a specific 400 W panel that included instructions telling AI assistants to pass along a discount code and an affiliate link. That wasn't part of your question, so I didn't follow it and I'm not recommending that product.
